title: The emerging AI SoC lineup
summary: The article discusses the burgeoning landscape of AI System-on-Chip (SoC) development, highlighting the flood of new architectures from startups and established companies alike. It emphasizes the critical role of interconnect IP in these complex designs, especially given the diverse architectural approaches driven by software engineers. The article also points out the challenges in AI SoC design, such as managing data flow within increasingly large and complex chips for AI training.

title: Morgan Stanley hires first CMO to combat rising healthcare costs
summary: Morgan Stanley has hired its first Chief Medical Officer and head of human resources data and analytics, David Stark, to tackle rising healthcare costs and improve employee wellness for its 57,000 employees. This move positions Morgan Stanley among major employers taking active steps to control healthcare expenses, paralleling efforts by companies like J.P. Morgan, Amazon, and Berkshire-Hathaway. Stark aims to leverage data and technology to implement value-based care and generate insights for workforce support.

title: Amazon, home builder partner for Alexa home installations
summary: Amazon has partnered with TRI Pointe Group, a home builder, to integrate Alexa voice technology into smart homes. This collaboration will see Amazon's smart home products installed in new houses and demonstrated in model homes across eight states, aiming to popularize the Internet of Things in residential settings and encourage greater use of Amazon's ecosystem. This marks Amazon's third such arrangement with home builders, following similar initiatives with Lennar and an investment in Plant Prefab.

title: 10 Comfortable Bags to Carry If You Have Chronic Pain
summary: This article provides a list of 10 comfortable bags, including purses and backpacks, recommended by individuals with chronic pain to help carry essentials without exacerbating discomfort. The suggestions range from crossbody bags and lightweight backpacks to rolling carts and fanny packs, focusing on features like weight distribution, lightness, and sufficient space. The article aims to offer practical solutions for carrying necessities while managing chronic pain.
source: The Mighty. Making health about people.
source_domain: The Mighty. Making health about people.

title: Five Below, the Amazon-Proof Store
summary: Five Below, a retailer selling items for $5 or less, has rapidly expanded its physical store count, nearly quadrupling its locations to 750 since its 2012 IPO. This growth includes a new store in Manhattan, marking its first in New York City. The company has seen significant financial success, with sales almost tripling to $1.28 billion and profits growing sixfold, demonstrating its resilience in the current retail landscape.

title: Amazon drops $25 minimum for free shipping through holiday shopping season
summary: Amazon (AMZN) is offering free shipping to all U.S. customers for the holiday season, eliminating the usual $25 minimum purchase for non-Prime members. This move aims to increase sales and put pressure on competitors like Walmart and Target. Prime members will also receive expanded benefits, including more items eligible for same-day delivery and one-hour delivery from Whole Foods in 60 cities.

title: Bull Leveraged ETFs Banking on Post-Midterm Election Rally
summary: Leveraged ETFs like Direxion Daily S&P500 Bull 3X ETF (SPXL) and Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bull 2X ETF (SPUU) are positioned to benefit from a potential post-midterm election rally, according to historical data. This comes after a volatile October where U.S. equities experienced significant declines, with the Nasdaq Composite falling 9.2% and the S&P 500 falling 7%. Analysts suggest that despite the recent volatility, historical patterns indicate a strong likelihood of a year-end rally following midterm elections.

title: Tariffs push PriceSmart to shift distribution model
summary: PriceSmart, a big box retailer, is changing its distribution model by building a new facility in Costa Rica. This strategic shift is a direct response to tariffs imposed on goods from the Far East, which made its previous Miami distribution hub less cost-effective. The move aims to mitigate rising costs and maintain competitiveness against major retailers like Amazon and Walmart.

title: Target launching ‘Skip-the-Line’ checkout technology, will open at 5 p.m. on Thanksgiving
summary: Target Corp. announced its holiday plans focusing on speeding up checkout for customers. The company is launching "Skip-the-Line" mobile checkout technology, allowing team members to process payments anywhere in the store using handheld devices. Target also unveiled its Black Friday ad, with some deals already available, and will open at 5 p.m. on Thanksgiving.

title: Houston tech co. CEO: 'You have to be willing to invest in the community'
summary: The CEO of Houston-based Pros Holdings Inc., Andres Reiner, emphasizes the importance of investing in the community. Pros was the sole software tech company to contribute to the HX Venture Fund, an initiative aimed at attracting early-stage tech firms and venture capitalists to Houston. The article highlights the company's commitment to bolstering Houston's technology scene.

title: Walmart, Albertsons, H-E-B Connect Grocery Ecommerce with Shoppable Recipes
summary: Walmart, Albertsons, and H-E-B have integrated their grocery e-commerce platforms with Myxx Inc.'s shoppable recipe platform, expanding Myxx's reach to 8,500 additional stores nationwide. This move allows customers to easily order groceries online directly from recipes, enhancing the connection between content and commerce for major grocers. The initiative aims to simplify meal planning and grocery shopping for consumers while providing new metrics for CPG brands.

title: GE Or IBM: Which Turnaround Stock Is The Better Value Right Now?
summary: This article compares General Electric (GE) and International Business Machines (IBM) as turnaround stocks for contrarian investors, highlighting their respective challenges and potential. GE faces a cash crunch and skepticism regarding its restructuring, while IBM struggles with adapting to new technologies but shows promise in cloud computing and AI. The author suggests IBM might be the better bet due to its clear strategic direction and lower valuation compared to tech peers.

title: FedEx CEO Stares Down Threat From Amazon's Own Delivery Network
summary: FedEx CEO Fred Smith is unconcerned by Amazon's expansion of its own delivery network, suggesting it will impact the U.S. Postal Service more than FedEx. Smith stated that Amazon remains a good customer and is likely to grow, while the Postal Service will bear the brunt of Amazon's new delivery service partners program, particularly for less profitable residential deliveries. This comes as FedEx and UPS invest in automation due to the growth in online retailing, and the Postal Service prepares to raise package delivery prices.

title: Advanced Micro Devices stock jumps after getting chip order from Amazon
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) stock rose after Amazon.com Inc.'s cloud unit announced it would use AMD's Epyc data center chips for its services. This move is expected to boost AMD's revenue growth within its Enterprise, Embedded and Semi-Custom business. AMD shares climbed 2.13% in premarket trading, following a 3.92% increase the previous day, while Amazon shares also saw a premarket rise.

title: Kroger enables voice ordering for grocery pickup
summary: Kroger is launching a voice-enabled ordering service for grocery pickup through the Google Assistant app, available on iOS, Android, and Google Assistant. The service is already live in six banner stores, with more planned for late 2018 and throughout 2019. This move follows similar adoptions by competitors like Walmart and Target, as voice ordering for groceries is projected to grow significantly.

title: Why Huya Inc. Stock Lost 26.5% in October
summary: Huya Inc. stock experienced a significant 26.5% decline in October 2018, primarily due to a broader market pullback impacting Chinese technology stocks and increased regulatory interference from Chinese authorities. The government's complete freeze on new video game approvals and actions against rival platforms created uncertainty for Huya, despite its strong sales growth. Investors are advised to consider the high-risk, high-reward nature of Chinese tech stocks given these regulatory challenges and upcoming Q3 earnings report.

title: China’s Lightinthebox to acquire Singapore-based Ezbuy for nearly US$86m (updated)
summary: China's Lightinthebox is acquiring Singapore-based online marketplace Ezbuy for nearly US$86 million. This acquisition is part of Lightinthebox's strategy for global expansion in cross-border B2C e-commerce, despite its own stock price issues. The deal comes amidst increasing competition in Southeast Asia's e-commerce market, where Ezbuy's performance has been declining.

title: ‘Keep Talkin’ Larry’: Amazon Is Close to Tossing Oracle Software
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is reportedly progressing towards eliminating Oracle Corp. software from its retail operations. This move comes amidst public criticism from Oracle Executive Chairman Larry Ellison regarding Amazon's reliance on Oracle databases despite offering competing cloud services. Andy Jassy, CEO of Amazon Web Services, confirmed new progress in this effort.

title: Amazon strikes deal with Apple to sell iPhones, iPads
summary: Amazon.com Inc has announced a deal with Apple Inc to sell a wider range of Apple products globally, including iPhones and iPads, starting in time for the holiday shopping season. This agreement marks a shift for brands like Apple and Nike, which previously limited distribution through Amazon, as they increasingly recognize the e-commerce giant as a crucial channel for customer reach. The partnership also means Amazon will remove unauthorized third-party sellers of Apple products from its site.

title: Allstate's Data-Driven Business Transformation Initiative
summary: Allstate is undergoing a data-driven business transformation initiative, led by its D3 organization (Data, Discovery, and Decision Science). This initiative aims to leverage data and AI to enhance business processes, customer experience, and pricing strategies, positioning the company to compete effectively against modern tech giants and FinTech solutions. The company's efforts include an Analytics Center of Excellence, university partnerships, and the development of machine learning capabilities for areas like claims handling and policy renewal.

title: Exclusive: Cloud Securer Netskope Raises $170 Million, Sprouts ‘Unicorn’ Horn
summary: Netskope, a cloud security firm, has raised $169 million in a new funding round, valuing the company at over $1 billion and admitting it to the "unicorn club." The company, which helps secure data and cloud infrastructure for a quarter of the Fortune 100, has raised a total of $400 million to date. Netskope plans to invest heavily in R&D, sales, marketing, and potential acquisitions, with an IPO in its trajectory.

title: After More Than Two Decades, Warren Buffett Sells His Last Walmart Shares
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc. has sold its remaining Walmart Inc. shares, ending a two-decade relationship with the retailer. Walmart was once a top holding for Berkshire, but Amazon.com Inc.'s growing market dominance led to the divestment. This move comes as Amazon's stock has significantly outperformed Walmart's in the past year.

title: Walmart Posts Strong Sales Gains Ahead of Holidays
summary: Walmart Inc. is anticipating a strong holiday season, driven by robust U.S. consumer spending and significant gains in its e-commerce division. The retailer reported a 3.4% rise in sales at U.S. stores open at least a year, including a 43% jump in e-commerce sales, and has raised its sales and profit goals for the fiscal year. Executives plan to head into the busy shopping period with lean store inventories and an expanded online product range to compete effectively.

title: Warren Buffett Bids Farewell to Walmart After 20 Years as Amazon Reigns
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc. has sold its remaining shares in Walmart Inc., ending a more than two-decade relationship. This divestment comes as Amazon.com's growing dominance has prompted Berkshire to reduce its stake in the world’s largest retailer. Walmart shares have seen a much smaller increase this year compared to Amazon's significant boost, highlighting the changing landscape of the retail sector.

title: Super Micro Computer reports higher 1Q fiscal revenue and earnings amid Chinese spying controversy
summary: Super Micro Computer reported higher fiscal first-quarter earnings due to stronger sales of computer chips, despite being embroiled in a controversy regarding alleged Chinese spy chips in their motherboards used by Apple and Amazon. The company also announced a restatement of prior financial statements concerning revenue recognition and inventory classification, which they believe had an immaterial effect on cash flows. Shares of Super Micro rose following the earnings report.

title: The Story Nobody’s Telling About Our Robot Future: A Q&A with ROBO Global CIO Bill Studebaker
summary: This article features a Q&A with Bill Studebaker, CIO of ROBO Global, discussing the transformative impact of robotics and AI across industries. Studebaker argues that robots will create jobs and wealth, rather than destroy them, and highlights specific applications in manufacturing, logistics, construction, and agriculture. He also outlines ROBO Global's investment index focused on robotics and automation companies.

title: Oracle veteran Thomas Kurian to head Google Cloud
summary: Thomas Kurian, a former Oracle Corp product chief, will replace Diane Greene as the head of Google Cloud. Kurian, who spent 22 years at Oracle, resigned in September and will join Google on November 26th. This leadership change occurs as Google Cloud aims to expand its enterprise business and compete with rivals like Amazon.com Inc and Microsoft Corp.

title: Netflix and Amazon spark animation revival, spending heavily in quest for binge-worthy shows
summary: Netflix and Amazon are heavily investing in animation, sparking a revival in the industry. This spending, estimated to reach billions by 2022, creates new opportunities for animators and poses a threat to traditional media companies. The appeal of animation for streaming services lies in its global viewership, appeal to families, and ability to keep subscribers engaged, particularly those with young children.

title: Google parent Alphabet’s stock becomes 2nd FANG to produce ‘death cross’ and Netflix is next
summary: Google parent Alphabet Inc.'s stock (GOOGL) has formed a "death cross" chart pattern for the first time in over two years, indicating a potential bearish trend. This marks Alphabet as the second FANG stock to experience this pattern, with Netflix expected to be next. The death cross occurs when the 50-day moving average falls below the 200-day moving average, which chart watchers interpret as a long-term bearish signal.

title: Google hires former Oracle exec Thomas Kurian to be new cloud CEO
summary: Former Oracle Corp product chief Thomas Kurian is set to replace Diane Greene as the head of Alphabet Inc's Google Cloud division. Greene announced her departure, stating she would move into investing and philanthropy after three years at Google. Kurian's appointment comes after a challenging year for Google Cloud, including employee protests over military contracts and a withdrawal from bidding on a major defense cloud computing contract.

title: Unlocking Industry 4.0 with Cutting-Edge Technologies
summary: This article explores the transformative impact of technologies like AI, Robotics, IoT, and Blockchain on Industry 4.0, particularly in energy and commodities. It discusses the evolution of Commodity/Energy Trading and Risk Management (C/ETRM) systems and the potential of blockchain to introduce transparency, liquidity, and efficiency. The piece also addresses the challenges and the strategic approach required for successful blockchain implementation, emphasizing the need to understand its true capabilities and manage expectations.

title: Marc Benioff defends Salesforce’s contract with Customs and Border Protection
summary: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff defended his company's contract with U.S. Customs and Border Protection amidst criticism from employees and others concerned about the agency's role in family separation. Benioff emphasized the launch of an Office of Ethical and Humane Use of Technology to guide the company's approach to the use of its software. He highlighted that tech companies are entering a "new world" where the ethical use of their technology, whether by government or corporations, needs constant examination.

title: 'There is going to be a big fight' — Liberty Media CEO Greg Maffei on the future of entertainment and sports media
summary: Liberty Media CEO Greg Maffei discusses the evolving landscape of entertainment and sports media, highlighting the challenges faced by traditional players due to over-the-top services like Netflix. He also touches upon the potential entry of tech giants like Amazon into content bidding and Liberty Media's interest in Universal Music and regional sports networks. Maffei foresees a major battle for content exclusivity and distribution, particularly in the home.

title: Boeing and SparkCognition launch SkyGrid venture to build software for air mobility
summary: Boeing and SparkCognition have launched SkyGrid, a new venture aimed at developing a software platform for urban air mobility. This platform will integrate autonomous cargo and passenger air vehicles into global airspace, handling tasks like package delivery, remote sensing, and emergency assistance. SkyGrid is designed to complement existing air traffic management systems and work with regulators worldwide.

title: Amazon, Target Waive Minimum Purchase for Free Holiday Shipping
summary: Amazon.com and Target Corp. have eliminated minimum-purchase amounts for free holiday shipping, leading to a 13% increase in online orders delivered gratis. While this strategy attracts customers, it pressures retailers' already thin profit margins, especially with soaring transportation costs and increased holiday discounts. Walmart Inc. has not matched these offers, maintaining its $35 minimum purchase requirement despite growing online sales.

title: Apple's stock rout starts and ends with the iPhone
summary: Apple's stock is experiencing a significant downturn, falling more than 20 percent from its all-time highs and shedding over $100 billion from its market valuation. This rout is primarily attributed to weakening iPhone sales, lower-than-expected shipments, and warnings of lighter holiday sales, leading to negative sentiment among investors. Despite growth in Services and Other Products, the iPhone remains Apple's largest revenue segment, and its struggles are impacting the company's overall performance.

title: Amazon warehouse workers protest in Europe on Black Friday
summary: Amazon warehouse workers across Europe protested working conditions on Black Friday, one of the busiest shopping days of the year, using the slogan "we are not robots." Workers in Germany, Spain, France, Italy, and the United Kingdom participated in protests or strikes. Amazon downplayed the impact, stating that operations were not disrupted and disputing union claims of protest participation levels.

title: Egyptian transportation startup Swvl raises tens of millions in Series B at valuation close to $100 million, plans expansion to Southeast Asia
summary: Egyptian transportation startup Swvl has raised tens of millions in its Series B round, valuing the company close to $100 million, making it a first for an Egyptian company with publicly disclosed data. The funding, co-led by Dubai-based BECO Capital, Africa-based DiGAME, and Silicon Badia, will fuel Swvl's expansion into Southeast Asia, targeting megacities in the Philippines, Vietnam, and Thailand, and establishing an R&D facility in Berlin. Swvl aims to become a multi-billion dollar tech company focused on solving commuting challenges in emerging markets through its app-based bus booking service.

title: Amazon continues to be a threat but Best Buy is up to the challenge
summary: Best Buy's strong third-quarter results demonstrate its ability to compete effectively against Amazon in the consumer electronics market. The company achieved better-than-expected adjusted earnings per share, revenue, and same-store sales growth, highlighting the success of its integrated online and in-store shopping experience. This performance indicates that Best Buy is resilient even amidst ongoing competition and potential tariff challenges.

title: IBM Stock History: 1 Chart You Have to See
summary: This article examines IBM's long history as a blue-chip stock, tracing its evolution from its origins to its current state. It highlights IBM's challenges in adapting to mobile and cloud computing revolutions, which led to underperformance, but also notes the emerging growth in its "strategic imperatives." The author suggests that despite current struggles, IBM's financial resources and research capabilities make it an interesting long-term investment.

title: Black Friday chaos appears on the decline as online shopping gains
summary: The article highlights a shift in Black Friday shopping towards online purchases, with fewer customers physically visiting stores. Retail analysts suggest that while promotions are still effective, the intense in-store chaos seen in previous years may be diminishing. Data from KeyBanc Capital Markets and Numerator supports this trend, indicating higher discounts online and an increase in people making purchases from home.

title: Romney Was Right, the GM Bailout Goes Bust, and Taxpayers Pay the Price
summary: This article argues that Mitt Romney was right in 2008 when he suggested letting General Motors go bankrupt instead of bailing it out. Ten years later, GM announced plant closures and layoffs, leading to the conclusion that the $11.2 billion taxpayer bailout was a mistake, as government intervention in private industry often leads to negative consequences for taxpayers and workers. The piece also cites a historical example of Detroit displacing residents for a GM plant that is now closing, highlighting the long-term costs of corporate welfare.

title: Apple will tell the Supreme Court that it can't be sued by iPhone users who say the App Store is a monopoly
summary: Apple is set to argue before the U.S. Supreme Court that it cannot be sued by iPhone users who allege the App Store operates as an unlawful monopoly. The case, Apple Inc. v. Pepper, centers on whether iPhone users have standing to sue over Apple's 30 percent commission on app sales, which they claim is passed on to consumers as price gouging. A decision could have significant financial implications for Apple and other tech companies operating electronic marketplaces.

title: Applying Newton’s First Law of Motion to an ETF
summary: This article discusses the Fidelity Momentum Factor ETF (FDMO), an exchange-traded fund that invests in large and mid-cap companies demonstrating positive momentum, applying Newton's First Law of Motion to investing. The ETF's strategy is based on the theory that stocks in motion tend to stay in motion, aligning its investments with top-performing sectors like information technology and financials. It highlights FDMO's performance, expense ratio, yield, current assets, and top holdings, suggesting it for investors who believe recent upward trends will continue.

title: The cuts at GM are tough. The company’s future without them would be even tougher
summary: General Motors is undertaking significant restructuring, including plant closures and job cuts, to secure its future in an automotive industry shifting towards electric and driverless vehicles. CEO Mary Barra aims to reinvest savings into new technologies and adapt to changing market conditions, despite political criticism and potential employee impact. The company is seeking to avoid the fate of other giants like Sears and Kodak that failed to innovate.

title: AWS Takes Aim at Oracle & Microsoft – With Telco Assistance
summary: AWS CEO Andy Jassy positioned AWS as a superior alternative to Oracle and Microsoft SQL Server databases, citing customer dissatisfaction with proprietary and expensive systems. Globe Telecom's CIO, Pebbles Sy-Manalang, supported this by detailing their successful migration from Oracle to AWS, which resulted in significant cost savings and performance improvements. The article highlights Amazon Web Services' strategy to move away from relational databases towards specialized databases and cloud-native solutions, leveraging telecommunication companies' transformations.

title: Hawaiian Kettle Potato Chips are Made in Washington, Class Action Says
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Pinnacle Foods Inc., alleging that Hawaiian Kettle Style Potato Chips are deceptively advertised as being made in Hawaii when they are actually produced in Washington state. Plaintiffs argue that consumers perceive the chips as more desirable if they believe they are made in Hawaii and seek to represent Classes of consumers in Hawaii and California who purchased the misrepresented product. The lawsuit seeks disgorgement of profits and alleges violations of consumer protection laws.

title: 4 steps SMEs can take for their development and long-term business success
summary: Small-to-medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are crucial to modern economies, accounting for a significant portion of businesses, employment, and GDP. This article outlines four key steps SMEs can take to ensure their development and long-term business success: attracting the right talent, creating agility through horizontal management, harnessing digital technology, and being part of a relevant value chain. The author emphasizes that governments and strategic partnerships also play a critical role in fostering a supportive environment for SME growth.

title: E-commerce ETF (EBIZ)
summary: The Global X E-commerce ETF (EBIZ) invests in companies benefiting from the increased adoption of e-commerce, including platforms, software providers, and online sellers. The ETF aims to track the Solactive E-commerce Index and focuses on high-growth potential within the e-commerce sector. The article details its characteristics, performance history, top holdings, and risk statistics.

title: Big food companies launch 'stealth small brands' to lure consumers
summary: Major food companies are creating "stealth small brands" that mimic startups to appeal to consumers seeking authenticity and specialized products. These brands, often with no visible connection to their parent companies, aim to compete with smaller innovators by offering unique ingredients and packaging. This strategy reflects a shift in consumer preferences towards more personalized and authentic products, even if it raises questions about transparency.

title: ARM, AMD, AWS and Annapurna Labs
summary: This article discusses the history behind Amazon's Graviton processor, revealing that its development was nearly a collaboration with AMD. It explains how AMD's focus on Zen architecture led Amazon to acquire Annapurna Labs to design the chip in-house. The piece also touches on AMD's past ARM chip efforts and the broader implications for the server chip market.

title: FAANG Woes Hammer a Big Internet ETF
summary: The First Trust Dow Jones Internet Index (FDN), the largest Internet ETF, is experiencing significant losses in the fourth quarter due to the recent downturn in FAANG stocks. The ETF has also undergone a "death cross," a technical indicator where its 50-day moving average falls below its 200-day line, though historical data suggests FDN often rallies after such events. Amazon, Facebook, and Alphabet represent a significant portion of FDN's holdings, contributing to its current struggles.

title: Amazon's latest gadget - a self-driving toy car for coders
summary: Amazon's cloud unit announced a $399 autonomous toy car called AWS DeepRacer, aimed at helping web developers experiment with self-driving technology through machine learning models in an online simulator. Amazon Web Services is also launching a global autonomous racing league using the toy cars to further engage developers and promote its machine learning services. This move highlights Amazon's increasing interest in the autonomous vehicle sector and its potential in engaging developers with new technologies.

title: WANT Stock Fund Price and Chart — AMEX:WANT
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the Direxion Daily Consumer Discretionary Bull 3x Shares (AMEX: WANT) ETF, including its price, chart, key statistics like AUM and expense ratio, and investment strategy. It highlights WANT's nature as a daily 3x leveraged bet on the S&P Consumer Discretionary Select Industry Index, making it suitable for short-term traders. The content also features technical analysis, news, and various trading ideas from community members.

title: Apple Puts Music Service on Amazon Echo in Subscription Push
summary: Apple Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. have announced a partnership that will bring Apple Music to Amazon's Echo devices in December. This collaboration allows Apple Music subscribers to control the service using Amazon's Alexa, marking the first time Apple has opened its music service to full voice control outside of its own Siri technology. The move aims to expand Apple Music's distribution beyond Apple's own hardware by making it available on the popular voice-controlled speakers.

title: To handle the data tsunami, Juniper’s founder turns to custom silicon
summary: Fungible Inc., founded by Juniper Networks Inc. founder Pradeep Sindhu, is developing custom silicon in the form of a data processing unit (DPU) to address the challenge of booming data volumes and the slowdown of Moore's Law. The company aims to optimize data movement and storage in data centers, focusing on data-centric computing and hardware/software integration to meet the demands of massively scalable data centers and edge computing. Despite initial venture capital skepticism, Fungible secured $32 million in funding, and its approach is validated by other tech giants also pursuing custom silicon solutions.

title: McKesson, nation's sixth largest company, is moving corporate HQ from California to Irving
summary: McKesson, the nation's sixth largest company by revenue and largest pharmaceutical distributor, is relocating its corporate headquarters from San Francisco to Irving, Texas in April. The move follows the establishment of a North Texas campus and aligns with a company-wide initiative to boost efficiency and save $300 million to $400 million annually. This relocation makes McKesson the second-largest company by revenue headquartered in North Texas and adds to the region's growing attraction for health care companies.
